# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_008_page_001.jpg

---

**1** She reaches mightily from one end to the other, and she orders all things well.

**2** I loved her and sought her from my youth; I desired to take her as my bride, and I became captivated by her beauty.

**3** She glorifies her noble birth by dwelling in intimacy with God, and the Master of all things has loved her.

**4** For she is an initiate into the knowledge of God, and she chooses his works.

**5** If riches are a desirable possession in life, what is richer than Wisdom who works all things?

**6** And if understanding is effective, who in all the world is a greater craftsman than she?

**7** And if one loves righteousness, the fruits of her labor are virtues; for she teaches self-control and prudence, justice and courage — and nothing in life is more useful to human beings than these.

**8** And if one desires wide experience, she knows the things of the past and discerns the things to come; she understands the subtleties of speech and the solutions of riddles; she has foreknowledge of signs and wonders, and the outcomes of seasons and times.

**9** I resolved therefore to take her to live with me, knowing that she would be a counselor of good things and a comfort in times of care and grief.

**10** On her account I will have glory among the multitudes, and honor before the elders, though I am young.

**11** I will be found keen in judgment, and in the sight of rulers I will be admired.

**12** When I am silent, they will wait for me; when I speak, they will pay attention; and when I speak at greater length, they will lay their hand upon their mouth.

**13** On her account I will have immortality, and leave behind an eternal memory for those who come after me.

**14** I shall govern peoples, and nations will be subject to me.

**15** Formidable rulers will be afraid of me when they hear of me; among the multitude I shall show myself good, and courageous in war.

**16** When I enter my house, I shall find rest beside her; for her companionship has no bitterness, and life with her brings no grief, but only gladness and joy.

**17** Reflecting on these things and turning them over in my heart — that immortality lies in kinship with Wisdom,

**18** and in her friendship is good delight, and in the labors of her hands is inexhaustible wealth, and in the exercise of fellowship with her is understanding, and great renown in sharing discourse with her — I went about seeking how I might take her for my own.

**19** I was a child of good natural disposition, and a good soul fell to my lot;

**20** or rather, being good I entered an undefiled body.

**21** But perceiving that I could not otherwise gain self-mastery unless God granted it — and even this recognition was itself a mark of wisdom, to know whose gift it is — I approached the Lord and besought him, and said with my whole heart:
